audit.whatIsWrong: The page called Sylas's E a 'chain-dash STUN' in six places and built the entire green-light system around it. Riot's text for Abscond / Abduct describes a dash plus a recast that throws chains and pulls Sylas to an enemy hit — it states no stun, and unlike every genuinely CC-carrying ability in this data set the entry carries no hardCC flag, only dash and projectile.
audit.why: The difference is what you do with W: against a stun you must hold Rune Prison purely reactively, against a 400-range pull you can pre-empt the gap-close. The page also never gave the ability's cooldown (13/12/11/10/9) or range (400), which is what makes 'punish the downtime' actionable.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, spikes[0].text, whys[1] and wants.foe[0] rewritten to describe the chain-pull with its real numbers, without asserting the absence of a stun either.

notes: The stun question needs a human ruling. Riot's Data Dragon text for Abscond / Abduct mentions only the dash and the chain-pull, and the derived flags list dash and projectile with no hardCC — two independent signals — so I removed the 'chain-stun' phrasing rather than repeat it. I did NOT write 'it does not stun' anywhere, because absence from Riot's text is not proof of absence in game, and this data explicitly warns that empty means unknown. Two further instances survive in fields I could not rewrite inside the length band: content 'early' ('he can E-stun into W burst') and full breakdown.cooldowns ('Dash into chain-stun'). If a human confirms there is no stun, those two need the same treatment; if there IS a stun, my five edits should be reverted.
